title: Shadow English Practice Day 2 | Daily Use English Sentences | Listen and Repeat for Beginners

sentences.t: Hello and welcome back to Leo English podcast.

And I'm Tina.
We are your hosts here.

You hear a sentence, then you repeat it like a shadow.

My alarm goes off at 6:30.

I check the weather before I leave.

I check the weather before I leave.
I check the weather before I leave.

I leave the house at 8:00.

I lock the door and check it twice.

I need to buy some milk and bread.

Where can I find the rice?

Please keep the change.

Nice. Group three.
Work. Your job, your tasks, your day.

I have three things on my list today.

Sentence 14. I start work at 9:00.
I start work at 9:00.

Work from home.

Let me write that down.
Let me write that down.

Sentence 17. I need a short break.
I need a short break.

Sentence 18.
Sentence 18. I finish my work at 5:00.

Sentence 19. Hello, can you hear me?
Hello, can you hear me?

Sentence 20. Sorry, I can't hear you well.
Sorry, I can't hear you well.

Can't is can plus not.

Sentence 21. I'll call you back in 10 minutes.
I'll call you back in 10 minutes.

Exactly. Call back is a very common phrasal verb.
Sentence 22. My phone is almost dead.
My phone is almost dead.

Exactly. Sentence 23.
I'm charging my phone.
I'm charging my phone and the thing I use is a charger, right?
Yes. Charger is the object.
Charging is the action.
Sentence 24. Send me a message when you get home.
Send me a message when you get home.

Send me a message when you get home.

Group five, at home.
Chores, my favorite word.

I do the dishes after dinner.

Careful with that one.
Ah, common mistake.
Do the dishes, wash the plates, same thing.
Exactly. Sentence 26.
I take out the trash.
I take out the trash.

Yes, you take the trash bag out of the house.
Trash is the rubbish.
Trash, rubbish, garbage.

I water my plants on Sunday.
I water my plants on Sunday.

Yes, to water is the action, like to email and to text.
English is funny.

Sentence 28.
Sentence 28. I put my keys on the table.

The living room is a little messy.

Messy means not clean and not organized.
Clothes on a chair.

My room looks like a small storm.
Sentence 31. I watch one episode before bed.
I watch one episode before bed.

Ah, so one episode is one piece, but I always watch four.
Everybody says that.
Sentence 32 I talk to my sister on the phone.
I talk to my sister on the phone.

Yes, on the phone, not in the phone.
Another common mistake.
On the phone, loud and clear.
Sentence 33 I read for 20 minutes.
I read for 20 minutes.

You set the time.

5:30, never again.
Sentence 35 I turn off the lights.
I turn off the lights.

Little words, big difference.

Next word, snooze.

A short sleep in the day is a nap.

Next word?
Size. It means how big or how small something is.

This shirt comes in three sizes, small, medium, and large.

Next word, list.
A list is a group of things you write down.
We heard it in sentence 13, I have three things on my list today.
For example, I write a shopping list every Saturday.
Please put milk on the list, and I never forget my list, except always.
One mistake. Students say I listed for I write it down.
So, I write things on a list.
I do not list things.
I will try to remember.
Next word, break.
A break is a short rest from work or study.
We heard it in sentence 17.
I need a short break.
For example, let's take a break after this meeting.
I take a break at 11:00 every morning, with tea, of course.
And careful, a break is a rest, but a broken is something damaged.
So, I take a break, and my old phone is broken.
Two different things.
Next word, charger.
A charger gives power to your phone.
We heard it in sentence 23.
I'm charging my phone.
And what is the difference between charge, charger, and charged?
Great question. Charge is the verb, charger is the object, and charged means full power.
So, my phone is charging, my charger is in my bag, and my phone is charged.
Next word, dishes.
The dishes are the plates, bowls, and cups for a meal.
We heard it in sentence 25.
I do the dishes after dinner.
And remember, we do the dishes, never make the dishes.
Ah, a mistake I made for years.
Make the dishes sounds like cooking.
Exactly. For example, it's your turn to do the dishes.
I did the dishes, and now I'm free.

Trash is the waste you throw away.
We heard it in sentence 26.
I take out the trash.
For example, please take out the trash before you leave.

I take out the trash twice a week.

I take it out when my sister visits.

Messy means not tidy and not organized.
We heard it in sentence 29.
